newsitem.title: CZECH REPUBLIC: Czech Deputy PM says govt mulls cabinet shuffle.
newsitem.headline: Czech Deputy PM says govt mulls cabinet shuffle.

text.p: Czech Deputy Prime Minister Josef Lux said on Wednesday that the government was considering a cabinet shuffle, but that no agreement had been reached.
Speaking at a briefing during a government meeting, Lux said that changes were being discussed, but gave no further details.

The government has come under heavy criticism recently after a wave of economic data showed the economy had slowed considerably, with industrial and construction output contracting in both January and February.
The economic daily Hospdarske Noviny, quoting unnamed sources, reported on Wednesday that some key ministers, including Finance Minister Ivan Kocarnik may be sacked.
Kocarnik's ministry has been sharply criticised for the current state of the capital markets, which investors say is opaque and poorly regulated.

Last week, Deputy Finance Minister Vladimir Rudlovcak, responsible for market oversight, resigned after several cases where Czech investment fund managers and major shareholders were found to have been stripping assets of the funds under the noses of regulators.
